name: Lornoxicam
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Lornoxicam is an oxicam nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) metabolized by CYP2C9; its pharmacokinetics change little in kidney failure, but NSAID effects on kidney blood flow still apply. The Irish label reduces dosing to once daily in kidney impairment and contraindicates it in severe impairment, defined by serum creatinine above 700 µmol/L. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The SmPC grades kidney impairment by serum creatinine: mild 150–300 µmol/L, moderate 300–700 µmol/L, severe above 700 µmol/L (about 7.9 mg/dL). Bands are mapped to creatinine clearance (CrCl) by judgment.

bands.recommendation: Usual (acute pain): 8 to 16 mg/day in 8 mg doses; day 1 may be 16 mg then 8 mg 12 hours later; maximum 16 mg/day after day 1 (SmPC).
Kidney impairment: reduce dosing frequency to once daily (SmPC). Use with caution; stop if kidney function worsens.
Kidney impairment: reduce dosing frequency to once daily (SmPC). Use with caution; stop if kidney function worsens.
Severe impairment (serum creatinine above 700 µmol/L): contraindicated (SmPC). Below that, once daily with caution. Our judgment: avoid at CrCl <15.

hd: Avoid: contraindicated in severe kidney impairment (SmPC). NSAIDs threaten residual kidney function.
pd: Avoid: contraindicated in severe kidney impairment (SmPC).
crrt: Avoid; NSAIDs worsen acute kidney injury.
monitoring: Kidney function in surgery, heart failure, diuretic or nephrotoxic co-therapy; stop if kidney function deteriorates. Hemoglobin, creatinine and liver enzymes regularly if used beyond 3 months (SmPC 4.4).

renal.recommendation: Not established in children; kidney dosing not applicable.

adult: Serum creatinine–based grading cannot be converted to CrCl reliably; mapping is a judgment. 700 µmol/L ≈ 7.9 mg/dL (arithmetic).
Retrieved SmPC is the 8 mg rapid tablet (acute pain only). PH also has 4/8 mg tablets and injection for arthritis; doses for OA/RA (12–16 mg/day) not covered.
SmPC 5.2 internally inconsistent on excretion split (50% feces/42% urine vs 2/3 liver, 1/3 kidney).
